newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam probes mysterious sinking near volcano.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam probes mysterious sinking near volcano.

text.p: Vietnamese scientists on Friday were investigating reports of land having sunk by up to three metres (10 feet) near a long-extinct volcano in the central highland province of Gia Lai.

An official with the state hydro-meteorology office told Reuters that experts had been sent to an area close to the Ham Rong (Dragon's Mouth) volcano to examine the sinking of several thousand square metres of land used for coffee crops.

He said ground around the sunken patches, some of which were several kilometres (miles) apart, was covered by small cracks. He said movement of underground gases was being investigated as a possible cause.
The ground began sinking during last year's rainy season, between September and November.
"Farmers have abandoned these crops. Local people say the dragon is moving its tail in anger," he said.
Newspaper reports said the volcano has been extinct for around 1,000 years.
